proposals.title: Adaptive Threshold Bearing Fault Detection Under Seasonal Temperature Variation in Wind Turbines
proposals.markdown:
## Adaptive Threshold Bearing Fault Detection Under Seasonal Temperature Variation in Wind Turbines

**Company:** Described problem works in renewable energy. [C999] Challenge C999-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Vladana Radić is a Full Professor in the Department of Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0822]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Vibration sensors on wind turbine gearboxes raise false alarms in cold weather, and bearing faults are still missed in winter despite fixed thresholds per season. [C999-CH1] The company holds two years of labelled vibration data from 40 turbines, and fixed seasonal thresholds fail to prevent missed bearing faults in winter. [C999-CH1]

### Research questions
1. Can a multivariate adaptive threshold model — trained on the labelled two-year dataset and conditioned on ambient temperature as a continuous covariate — reduce false-alarm rate in cold-weather months while keeping missed-fault rate at or below the warm-weather baseline? Measured by precision and recall on held-out winter quarters versus summer quarters of the labelled dataset.
2. Can an adaptive, season-aware fault classifier reduce false alarms in winter while maintaining detection of genuine bearing faults, compared with the current fixed-threshold approach? Measured by false-alarm rate and missed-fault rate on the labelled vibration dataset, split by season.

### Approach
- Extract time-domain and frequency-domain features (RMS, kurtosis, envelope spectrum bands) from the labelled vibration records and build a seasonal baseline per bearing location to distinguish operating-condition variation from fault-driven signal change.
- Apply PCA and Hotelling T² multivariate statistical process control to model the normal operating region as a function of temperature, so that the control boundary shifts continuously with environmental conditions rather than by fixed seasonal step.
- Adapt the patent's adaptive threshold mechanism to use temperature as an additional operating-condition covariate alongside rotational speed, and calibrate threshold trajectories on the warm-weather data before validating on held-out winter data.
- Evaluate the adaptive classifier against the fixed-threshold baseline on the labelled vibration dataset, reporting precision, recall, and false-alarm counts per season.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from Radić's group, guided by Radić and supported by the company's condition monitoring engineer at roughly one day per week, ingests and audits the two-year dataset: aligns timestamps, checks label consistency, and produces a clean feature matrix with temperature as a covariate for all 40 turbines. | A documented, labelled feature dataset ready for modelling, with a baseline false-alarm and missed-fault count per season using the company's current threshold. |
| Months 4–6 | The student implements PCA + Hotelling T² control charts with temperature-conditioned boundaries and the adaptive threshold mechanism; Radić reviews model design. Experiments compare vibration-only and vibration-plus-temperature fusion across all four failure modes on held-out winter quarters. | A validated prototype model with precision, recall, and false-alarm metrics per season; a short technical report and a draft journal paper submitted for review. |

### First six months
- Month 1: The company transfers the two-year labelled vibration dataset to the university under a signed data-sharing agreement; the master's student sets up the feature extraction and seasonal segmentation pipeline.
- Month 2: The student and the company engineer audit label consistency across all 40 turbines and agree on a train/validation/test split that holds out at least one full winter quarter.
- Month 3: Baseline metrics (false-alarm rate, missed-fault rate by season) are computed on the current fixed-threshold system, establishing the target the adaptive model must beat.
- Months 4–6: Radić's adaptive threshold and PCA-T² methods are implemented and tuned on training data; results on the held-out winter test set are compared against the baseline and reported to the company.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Two years of labelled vibration data from 40 turbines, available for the project. [C999-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Radić holds a granted patent on adaptive threshold setting for vibration-based bearing condition monitoring under variable operating speed. [SYN-PAT-045] Radić co-authored work on multivariate statistical process control using PCA and Hotelling T² for simultaneous monitoring of multiple bearing locations in rotating machinery. [SYN-PUB-08930] Radić co-authored work on sensor fusion combining vibration and thermal data for early fault detection in rolling element bearings across multiple failure modes. [SYN-PUB-08927] Radić is open to joint projects with process industry companies and to contract research for condition monitoring system development and validation. [R0822]

### Why this pair
The company has a clearly bounded signal-processing problem and two years of labelled data that make it solvable within six months — the data asset removes the usual first-year collection risk. Radić brings the three specific technical pieces the problem requires: an adaptive threshold patent that targets variable operating conditions, a multivariate control-chart method that can absorb temperature as a continuous covariate, and sensor-fusion work that jointly models vibration and thermal signals. The company brings two years of labelled turbine vibration data and operational ground truth on fault events; Radić brings adaptive threshold methods, multivariate statistical process control applied to rotating machinery, and sensor fusion of vibration and thermal signals.

- The company's problem is that fixed seasonal thresholds fail to prevent missed bearing faults in winter; Radić is named as an inventor on a granted patent on adaptive threshold setting for vibration-based bearing condition monitoring under variable operating speed. [C999-CH1, SYN-PAT-045]
- Radić co-authored work on multivariate statistical process control using PCA and Hotelling T² for simultaneous monitoring of multiple bearing locations in rotating machinery. [SYN-PUB-08930]
- Radić co-authored work on sensor fusion combining vibration and thermal data for early fault detection in rolling element bearings across multiple failure modes. [SYN-PUB-08927]

### Risks and constraints
- The patent on adaptive threshold setting (SYN-PAT-045) covers variable operating speed; the company's core problem is seasonal temperature variation, and coverage of temperature as a covariate in that patent is not confirmed by the available record. [SYN-PAT-045, C999-CH1]
- The infrared thermography and thermal fusion work (SYN-PUB-08929, SYN-PRJ-0441) covers slow-speed bearings in conveyor and grain handling systems; applicability to wind turbine gearbox speeds would need to be assessed. [SYN-PUB-08929, SYN-PRJ-0441]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: results may be submitted for publication after a 45-day review period by the company; turbine-identifying details are removed or anonymised before submission.
- Ownership: the company owns the trained models and calibrated thresholds produced in the project; the university retains the right to use the general methods and non-proprietary results for further research.
- Data access: the company provides the labelled dataset under a signed data-sharing agreement before month 1 begins; the dataset is stored on university infrastructure accessible only to the named project team.
- Preconditions: the project starts upon execution of the data-sharing agreement and confirmation of the company engineer's availability for at least one day per week during the six-month period.

### Sources
- C999: Described problem
- C999-CH1: Our vibration sensors on wind turbine gearboxes raise false alarms in cold weather.
- R0822: Vladana Radić
- SYN-PAT-045: Method and Device for Adaptive Threshold Setting in Vibration-Based Bearing Condition Monitoring Under Variable Opera... (2020)
- SYN-PRJ-0441: Fusion of Vibration and Infrared Thermography Data for Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Industrial Machinery (2018)
- SYN-PUB-08927: Simultaneous Vibration and Surface Temperature Monitoring of Rolling Element Bearings: Correlation and Complementarity (2013)
- SYN-PUB-08929: Thermal Imaging-Based Condition Assessment of Slow-Speed Roller Bearings in Conveyor Systems (2016)
- SYN-PUB-08930: Multivariate Statistical Process Control for Simultaneous Monitoring of Multiple Bearing Locations in Rotating Machinery (2017)

claim.text: Fault classification and remaining useful life prediction for power electronics using gradient boosting, survival models, and LSTM networks on vibration and SCADA data.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08182 covers fault classification using random forest (not gradient boosting) on SCADA data for PV inverters; SYN-PUB-02957 covers gradient-boosted survival models and remaining useful life-adjacent maintenance scheduling on vibration and SCADA data; SYN-PUB-08184 covers LSTM for remaining useful life prediction on SCADA data — but the claim attributes gradient boosting to fault classification, which is not stated (gradient boosting in SYN-PUB-02957 is for survival/maintenance scheduling, not fault classification), so the claim merges methods across records incorrectly by implying gradient boosting is used for fault classification.

claim.text: Provided a six-month consultancy to a regional solar asset management company in 2022–2023 on automated performance reporting system specification and implementation.

rejected.reason: R0738 states that Starčević provided a six-month consultancy to a regional solar asset management company in 2022–2023 on the specification and partial implementation of an automated performance reporting system, but the claim says 'specification and implementation' whereas the record says 'specification and partial implementation', overstating the scope.

claim.text: Vibration-based bearing fault detection and classification using accelerometer arrays and time-frequency analysis on embedded microcontrollers.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-00585 covers embedded microcontroller deployment with 1D-CNN (no accelerometer arrays or time-frequency analysis); SYN-PUB-00584 covers MEMS accelerometer and SVM (no arrays or time-frequency analysis); neither publication mentions accelerometer arrays or time-frequency analysis, though R0045 mentions these in the bio context; the claim bundles these together as if all three publications support all named methods, but no single cited record combines accelerometer arrays with time-frequency analysis on microcontrollers.

claim.text: Remaining useful life prediction for bearings and cutting tools using deep learning and time-domain feature analysis.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-00593 covers LSTM (deep learning) for remaining useful life prediction of bearings, but SYN-PUB-00594 uses time-domain features with support vector regression (not deep learning) for cutting tool RUL; the claim says 'deep learning and time-domain feature analysis' as if both methods apply to both topics, but deep learning is not used in SYN-PUB-00594 and time-domain feature analysis is not the primary method in SYN-PUB-00593.

claim.text: Co-authored a wireless sensor node design validated through a 14-month field deployment at a food processing facility with three bearing faults detected and confirmed by maintenance staff.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-00589 lists Bogdan Bajić (R0045) as an author and describes a 14-month field deployment at a food processing facility monitoring eight conveyor-drive bearings, with three developing bearing faults flagged and confirmed by scheduled inspection; however, the record does not state the faults were 'confirmed by maintenance staff' — it says 'confirmed by scheduled inspection'.

claim.text: Experimental characterisation of rotating machinery on dedicated test rigs with 24-channel NI data acquisition, torque sensors, incremental encoders, and accelerometers at sampling rates to 65.5 kHz.

rejected.reason: "24 channel" and "NI" are not in SYN-PUB-05996 or SYN-PUB-00312 but are in R0510, which the claim does not cite.

claim.text: Operating-condition-dependent threshold setting for vibration-based fault detection under varying load and temperature, including fixed statistical and machine learning approaches.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-05999 covers threshold setting under varying load and temperature including fixed statistical and machine learning approaches, but SYN-PUB-05997 concerns tooth profile errors and detection thresholds based on manufacturing quality grade — it does not address varying load or temperature conditions, so the citation conflates two separate topics and the claim merges them into one scope.

claim.text: Passive vibration isolation platform design using wire-rope isolators with lumped-parameter modelling for precision measurement systems.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-03481 describes a passive vibration isolation platform using four wire-rope isolators with a lumped-parameter model, but the platform is designed for a machine-vision camera on a CNC milling machine, not for 'precision measurement systems' as the claim states — however 'precision measurement systems' is a reasonable direct inference from a machine-vision camera application and the paper's framing around measurement accuracy (MTF50 improvement), making this borderline; nonetheless the cited text explicitly frames it as a camera isolation platform, not broadly 'precision measurement systems', so the claim slightly widens the scope.

claim.text: Kernel methods for nonlinear process monitoring, including kernel principal component analysis applied to sensor data from manufacturing systems.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08486 covers kernel PCA applied to sensor data from manufacturing benchmark datasets, and SYN-PUB-08485 covers the generalised likelihood ratio test for covariance shifts in sensor arrays — SYN-PUB-08485 does not cover kernel PCA or kernel methods for nonlinear process monitoring, so citing it for 'kernel methods for nonlinear process monitoring' is not supported by its text.

claim.text: Led a cross-border Interreg project delivering SPC algorithm design and embedded deployment modules for IoT middleware on Cortex-M microcontrollers, with three completed pilot deployments in manufacturing.

rejected.reason: SYN-PRJ-0671 states it is a cross-border Interreg project with R0773 as work package leader on SPC algorithm design and embedded deployment with modules certified to run on Cortex-M class microcontrollers, with three completed pilot deployments — however, the claim says R0773 'led' the project, whereas the record states R0773 was 'work package leader', not the overall project leader; also 'IoT middleware' is accurate but the claim's framing as 'led a cross-border Interreg project' overstates the role described.

claim.text: Multi-class fault classification using supervised machine learning (support vector machines, random forests, convolutional neural networks) on spectral and spectrogram features.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08174 covers support vector machines, SYN-PUB-08172 covers random forests on envelope spectrum features, and SYN-PUB-08178 covers CNNs on spectrograms for fault classification, but none of these records mentions 'spectral features' as a shared input — SYN-PUB-08174 uses physics-informed amplitude ratio features, SYN-PUB-08172 uses envelope spectrum features, and SYN-PUB-08178 uses spectrograms; the claim bundles all three classifiers as using 'spectral and spectrogram features,' which overstates SYN-PUB-08174 (which uses kinematic/amplitude-ratio features, not raw spectral features) and merges separate points.

claim.text: Physics-informed feature engineering that embeds kinematic and geometric constraints into classifier input spaces for gearbox diagnosis.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08174 explicitly covers physics-informed feature engineering embedding kinematic constraints (gear mesh relationships, sideband spacing set to shaft frequency) into an SVM classifier input space for gearbox diagnosis, but SYN-PUB-08177 covers gear wear monitoring using TSA residual signals and makes no mention of physics-informed feature engineering or embedding kinematic/geometric constraints into classifiers.

claim.text: Installed and calibrated vibration monitoring hardware on an operating wind turbine in Vojvodina and interpreted field alarm events over two years as work package leader in a cross-border project.

rejected.reason: SYN-PRJ-0429 confirms R0737 as work package leader in a cross-border project with field installations on turbines in Vojvodina, and SYN-PUB-08173 confirms installation of accelerometers/tachometers on a wind turbine in Vojvodina with data collected over 18 months; however, the claim states 'two years' of alarm event interpretation, while SYN-PUB-08173 covers only 18 months and SYN-PRJ-0429 does not specify a two-year monitoring duration for alarm interpretation — the WINDMON project ran 2018–2020 (two years) but the record does not state two years of alarm event interpretation specifically.

claim.text: Remaining useful life prediction for rolling bearings using particle filters, LSTM networks, and Gaussian process regression on accelerometer-derived health indices.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08928 covers particle filters for RUL of gearbox bearings using RMS as health index; SYN-PUB-00593 covers LSTM for RUL of rolling bearings; SYN-PUB-02480 covers Gaussian process regression as one of seven benchmarked prognosis approaches for pump bearings — but none of the three sources mentions 'accelerometer-derived health indices' as a unifying thread, and critically, SYN-PUB-08928 uses RMS of a high-frequency band (not explicitly 'accelerometer-derived' as a combined claim), while no single source combines all three methods (particle filters, LSTM, GPR) on 'rolling bearings using accelerometer-derived health indices'; SYN-PUB-08928 is about gearbox bearings specifically, not rolling bearings generally, and SYN-PUB-02480 is a benchmarking preprint where GPR is one of seven methods, not a method the researcher developed — the claim overstates the scope by merging three separate works into a single unified capability statement and calls them all for 'rolling bearings' when SYN-PUB-08928 specifically concerns gearbox bearings.

claim.text: Bearing fault detection and classification via vibration signal envelope spectrum analysis, time-domain statistical features, and high-frequency band kurtosis.
